Our client is a fast-growing international software company. It is a global leader in its field and is growing by more than 25% every year. The company has the ambition to more than triple in size over the next four to five years. The company is owned by a private equity fund and is anonymous in this advertisement. To lead sales performance and lead generation, we are now looking for a

Head of Growth

High impact – Growth journey – Sales performance

Do you want to be the right hand of the CEO, with overall responsibility for sales performance and lead generation across an international group? And do you want to be a close sparring partner for both the CEO and the private equity owner while the company sets out to more than triple in size?

As Head of Growth you take on a central, high-impact role, where you lead sales teams and inside sales teams together with the country heads. You will own the full lead life cycle: you build and run performance management across the funnel (lead generation, MQLs, SQLs and conversion) and you are also accountable for generating MQLs and SQLs, as the Lead Generation Manager reports directly to you. You measure the effectiveness of marketing, inside sales and sales through pipeline reporting against budget at group, country and individual level.

The role is international and requires a presence within the EU. The location is flexible within Denmark.

Reporting to the Group CEO, your responsibilities will include:

• Own lead generation: lead and develop the Lead Generation Manager and be accountable for the volume and quality of MQLs and SQLs delivered to the sales teams

• Adapt, refine and align the sales funnel and sales process across business units, enabling best-practice sharing and sales problem-solving (knowledge of HubSpot and sales operations is a benefit)

• Drive sales team performance by instilling a culture of accountability, motivation and resilience, and by challenging the teams to achieve more

• Test new sales approaches, refine pitches and explore new methods

• Build a high-performing sales culture and develop the company’s sales playbook, including training, motivation and team development

• Scale sales strategies across multiple European markets and roll out a consistent playbook while allowing for local differences

• Act as a close sparring partner to the CEO and the private equity owner, including performance reporting and follow-up

To succeed in the role, you have 5–15 years of sales experience as both a sales rep and a sales manager, ideally in B2B SaaS or SME-focused sales. You are a high-energy, hands-on, front-line leader who thrives in high-growth environments and who regularly motivates, coaches and develops sales teams to top performance. You are comfortable with modern sales tools and can work across many stakeholders, including a private equity owner. You are fluent in English, and German is an advantage.

You are highly analytical and performance-driven, curious, and thorough when it comes to process and detail. You are known for your energy, your ability to bring people with you and your willingness to stand your ground.

Anonymity, private equity ownership and NDA

The company is anonymous in this advertisement and is owned by a private equity fund. As the role involves close and ongoing interaction with the fund, it is important to us that you know about the ownership structure from the start. We work with an NDA (non-disclosure agreement). The first conversation with Sensu takes place without an NDA. Before you meet the company, you sign an NDA, after which you receive full information about the company, its ownership and the role.

Are you our new Head of Growth? Then please upload your application and CV. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, sexuality, ethnicity and religion. For further information about the position, please contact Thomas Bech, CEO at Sensu, on +45 22 89 89 76.

Please note that we do not work with application deadlines, as applications are processed on a rolling basis.

**Job Description

**

Global Business Development Manager

Posting Start Date: 10/8/26

Gentofte, DNK, 2820,

Location: Copenhagen, Denmark

Working hours: Full-time

Work model: Hybrid

Contract type: Permanent

**About The Role

**We are excited to offer an incredible opportunity for a Business Development Manager to join Scandinavian Tobacco Group’s growing Next Generation Products team. In this pivotal role, you will be essential in supporting our innovative ventures beyond tobacco, using strategic insights and a strong understanding of global market trends. Moreover, you will be responsible for shaping and managing our global product portfolio while identifying strategic business opportunities to drive global growth. You will work cross-functionally to deliver and execute portfolio strategies & business development opportunities that help grow our brands and company.

Your role as a self-reliant professional is crucial in our fast-paced environment. A key part of your role will involve ensuring clear communication and alignment within the organization, while fostering robust professional relationships. You will be reporting to the Head of Business Development.

**WHAT WILL YOU BE RESPONSIBLE FOR?

****Lead Category Development

**

• Develop and implement comprehensive strategies for next generation products, ensuring alignment with consumer preferences and market trends.

• Analyzing market trends, consumer preferences, and competitor activities to identify opportunities and threats for the brand and category portfolio to improve performance & profitability.

• Evaluate the performance of the portfolio and adjust as needed to ensure it continues to deliver growth and profitability.

**Business Growth & Development

**

• Identify and evaluate new business opportunities, including market expansions, strategic partnerships, and potential acquisitions.

• Lead cross-functional teams to develop and execute business development initiatives that accelerate revenue growth and expand market presence.

• Leverage data and market insights to continuously evolve the product portfolio, ensuring the company remains ahead of industry trends.

• Utilize market research and consumer insights for the development of the next generation products portfolio strategy and to define its role and roadmap.

**Global Collaboration

**

• Work closely with regional and local teams to adapt portfolio strategies to local market needs and ensure the successful global rollout of new products.

• Ensure a cohesive approach to portfolio management and business development across markets, driving synergies and efficiencies globally.

**New Business Opportunities

**

• Identify and assess emerging trends and consumer needs to develop new product categories that align with the company's strategic goals.

• Lead the exploration and validation of new business ideas through market research, pilot programs, and feasibility studies.

• Develop business cases for new category initiatives, including market analysis, financial projections, and risk assessments.

• Collaborate with R&D, marketing, and sales teams to bring new product categories from concept to market launch.

• Establish strategic partnerships and alliances to support the development and growth of new categories.

• Monitor and evaluate the performance of new categories, making data-driven adjustments to ensure their success and profitability.

**WHAT SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE WILL BE REQUIRED?

**

• 3-5 years of experience in business development and/or project management, ideally within multinational FMCG companies. Global/regional experience is preferred.

• Strong analytical skills and strategic thinking with a track record of identifying and capitalizing on growth opportunities.

• Deep understanding of consumer behaviour, what drives their decisions and how we can adjust our strategies to fit their needs and expectations.

• Excellent project management skills, with experience leading cross-functional teams & influence senior stakeholders.

• Strong communication and relationship-building abilities across diverse global teams.

• Good Excel and PowerPoint skills and proven experience in utilizing data analytics tools.

• Fluency in English and ability to travel up 10-15% of the time.

**Hands-on Game Director for WHAT THE CAR?

**Do you love working in small, creative teams turning wild ideas into a reality? Do you thrive on community feedback? Could you ensure an already loved comedy game remains goofy in all the right ways? Awesome. We need to talk!

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

WHAT THE CAR? is our absurdly silly racing adventure game which addresses fundamental questions such as… What if a car had legs? Or a jetpack? Or secretly identified as a sailboat? First launched in 2023 on Apple Arcade and now also on Steam, it has gained a steady following of dedicated fans who have contributed hundreds of thousands of community-built levels.

We’re looking for a Game Director to grab the creative wheel (sorry) on a small but mighty team to help steer CAR into the future. You’ll guide decisions on which jokes are worth pursuing, how we maintain and push quality and which turns to take along the road. You'll work closely with studio creative leadership and external partners to help define the future of CAR and to explore opportunities to reach even bigger audiences.

If you’re already rethinking what a car is, keep reading!

**Here’s What You'll Do Day To Day

**

• Take product responsibility for WHAT THE CAR? and ensure that it remains true to and evolves upon the existing WHAT THE? universe

• Along with studio leadership, define the game’s ongoing vision, strategy and goals

• Effectively communicate the vision within the team to enable team and individual autonomy

• Work closely with the Producer and team to create achievable product roadmaps built upon a humanistic approach to production

• Contribute directly to project development, such as creating prototypes, implementing gameplay or building levels in-engine

• Facilitate team-wide creative processes which ensure all ideas have been heard and the best solutions are agreed and understood

• Ensure we maintain a high quality bar across the game, and help catch what’s not working before it ships

• Be part of nurturing a creative, inclusive, high performing, high trust team culture

• Immerse yourself in user feedback, turning what players tell us into decisions about where the game goes next

**You’re a great match if

**

• You bring 8+ years working in creative product lead roles

• You’ve worked on at least 3 commercial and shipped game projects

• You are extremely familiar with one or more commercial game engines, including Unity

• You're a born communicator and collaborator who enjoys working closely with every member of a team

• You understand and appreciate the WHAT THE? universe and are excited to be an integral part of its future

• You use AI to boost workflows and productivity, giving you more time to focus on the important creative decisions

• You prefer to “show don’t tell” by demonstrating ideas through prototypes over endless design discussions

• You have experience working on family-friendly titles for a casual audience

**Nice to have

**

• Experience coding in C#

• Experience with game design for a live game

• Experience in the mobile premium space

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**

• You thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forward

• You’re motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness and creativity while actively contributing to sustaining that culture

• You believe games are made by teams, not rockstars and that great ideas can come from anyone

• You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them

• You love exploration and experimentation but don’t get too precious when the evidence tells you you’re wrong

• You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place to be

**Practicalities

**

• Role based in our cozy office in central Copenhagen

• We want to make sure we find the right person, so we also consider people located outside of Denmark and provide financial (and moral!) relocation support

• This team works with an office-first hybrid model: primarily working together in office with occasional remote working

• We work a 37-hour work week with flexible working hours

• Our working language is English

**We offer

**

• The opportunity to define and shape the future of a beloved game together with a closely knit team where everyone is actively participating in the creative process

• A playful work environment where trying the silly idea is encouraged

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, and whatever else Tribanders turn into a tradition

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant, with plant-based options and soft ice on Thursdays

• Private health insurance paid by us

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked

• Endless amounts of Club Mate

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?

**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide.

From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make people laugh. We explore comedy through gameplay, which means we like to break player expectations, create surprising interactions, use great music and slick art, and build quirky worlds full of personality.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games. And we believe diversity makes teams better. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and who are excited to challenge us and our way of doing things.

Architect the future Finance platform that will power our global growth!

You will:

Apply today and help us shape the technology foundation of tomorrow. Send us your resume in English and help us design the solutions of tomorrow. Interviews will be scheduled on an ongoing basis.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

As a Machine Learning Engineer at Veo you will get to work on challenging problems and directly contribute to the value created by our AI-driven end-user products.

You will become part of our AI team, which comprises 20+ researchers and engineers responsible for all stages in the machine learning lifecycles across different projects - from scoping and defining data annotation tasks to modeling, validation, and deployment. You will be free to determine the directions of the project you work on while also getting feedback and being encouraged to spar with the rest of the team to assist each other in improving and succeeding.

We stay current with the latest research and continuously discuss concepts and ideas in recent papers to assess their relevance to our tasks and product-specific challenges.

We are looking to add yet another ambitious, high-performing junior to mid-level engineer or/researcher with proven experience from real-world machine learning projects to the team. Experience with computer vision is advantageous but not a must.

**What you will do:

**

• Train state-of-the-art machine learning models

• Write efficient inference pipelines for cloud and edge

• Define and supervise data annotation tasks

• Improve evaluation schemes to increase understanding of model performance and shortcomings

• Contribute to long-term planning and prioritization of tasks

**What you will need:

**

• MSc or PhD in a relevant field

• Hands-on experience with real-world, large-scale machine-learning projects

• Great coding skills

• Skilled at both autonomous tasks and contributing to group efforts

• Ability to examine details closely and critically

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

outcomes.

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

Actona Group operates in a dynamic and fast-changing commercial environment, where access to relevant data and the ability to translate it into actionable insights are increasingly important for commercial decision-making. As part of the Pricing & Commercial Excellence team, you will take on a central role in strengthening the commercial organisation through pricing, analytics, performance management and the continued development of commercial tools and processes.

The position combines a strong analytical and hands-on focus with the opportunity to contribute to the broader development of Commercial Excellence across Actona Group.

In this role, you will work at the intersection of data, pricing and commercial decision-making. A key responsibility will be to understand Actona’s pricing model in depth, take ownership of the technical solution behind it and ensure that management decisions related to pricing are effectively implemented. Alongside this, you will identify, collect and analyse relevant commercial data and turn your findings into concrete recommendations and initiatives. You will work with both structured and unstructured data, which calls for an investigative mindset and the ability to find relevant information even when it is not readily available.

At the same time, you will contribute to Actona’s broader Commercial Excellence agenda by developing and evaluating tactical commercial initiatives, supporting performance management and continuously improving the tools and processes that strengthen commercial execution.

Key responsibilities include:

• 
Maintain and further develop Actona’s pricing model and technical pricing solution

• 
Develop analyses, scenarios and decision-support tools to support commercial and pricing decisions

• 
Analyse price and margin development and identify commercial opportunities, risks and areas requiring action

• 
Translate commercial data and insights into concrete initiatives and recommendations

• 
Develop and analyse tactical commercial campaigns and follow up on their commercial impact

• 
Support commercial performance management by identifying opportunities, gaps and areas of underperformance

• 
Prepare clear and decision-oriented material for commercial management and relevant stakeholders

• 
Continuously develop analytical tools, methods and Commercial Excellence processes

• 
Explore how AI and other digital solutions can support commercial analyses, processes and decision-making

• 
Contribute to the implementation of a new CRM system, helping shape commercial processes and strengthen the use of data and insights across the organisation

Success in the role means that you are able to turn complex commercial information into analyses and recommendations that create value for the sales organisation. You drive and coordinate commercial initiatives across the organisation and locations, help sales directors focus and prioritise through relevant analyses, and ensure that pricing decisions are translated accurately and efficiently into the pricing model and commercial execution.

You have experience from areas such as pricing, Commercial Excellence, business analytics, BI, strategy, consulting or finance. You are comfortable working hands-on with data and commercial analysis and, importantly, know how to turn complex information into clear, actionable insights for commercial organisation.

You hold a relevant Master’s degree within engineering, mathematics, economics, business, finance or a similar field. You are highly proficient in Excel and experienced with Power BI or comparable BI tools, and you are comfortable working with complex datasets and developing analytical solutions. An interest in AI and emerging digital tools is an advantage. You are fluent in Danish and English, both written and spoken, and you communicate insights clearly to different audiences.

You are curious, commercially minded and able to create structure in a dynamic environment. You collaborate effectively across stakeholders, communicate clearly and maintain progress as priorities shift.

Actona’s culture is defined by three core values: Acceleration, Customer-Centricity and Trust. They believe in responsibility, collaboration and continuous improvement – and offer a work environment where people are encouraged to challenge, learn, and grow. You will get to work closely with decision-makers, contribute to strategic initiatives, and help shape how data is used across a global organisation.

Location: Holstebro

Travel: Up to 15 days per year

Take the next step in your career

Actona is collaborating with GML on this recruitment. If you have any questions about the position, please contact Researcher Kenny Byriel Thimsen at kt@gml-hr.dk. All inquiries will be treated confidentially.

Actona Group is an international furniture company headquartered in Holstebro, Denmark, with operations in more than 90 countries and production facilities across Europe and Asia. Rooted in strong entrepreneurial values, we combine commercial drive, speed of execution and a pragmatic mindset.

jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a postdoc position in the field of the intellectual history of corporate politics at the Department of Business Humanities and Law. The expected starting date is 1 May, 2027 or as agreed upon by consultation. The postdoc position is a non-tenured full-time position of 2 years, with the possibility of 1 additional year of teaching obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The postdoc project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

The research conducted will be team-based and oriented towards delivering on the project objectives. Taking the project framework into consideration, applicants are required to outline their reflections on how to approach the study.

The position is mainly in-place. The candidate should be able to be regularly present and attend meetings in Copenhagen.

For more information about the position, please contact PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen (mhj.bhl@cbs.dk). 

Research environment
The Department of Business Humanities and Law is dedicated to an integrated approach to the contemporary challenges facing business and society drawing on the humanities, interdisciplinary social sciences, and law. The core research areas of the Department of Business Humanities and Law are organized into different research Units: Governance, Culture and Learning; Entrepreneurship, Ethics and Leadership; and CBS Law. Faculty within these groups have research backgrounds in areas of political science, sociology, philosophy, history, anthropology, law, theology, aesthetics, design and innovation, tourism and leisure management, cultural economics, leadership and strategy, pedagogic study, and other areas. What unites faculty in our department is an overriding concern for the organization of the human within its multiple environments: work, nature, economy, civil association, the state, and corporation. 

Teaching responsibilities of the Department comprise undergraduate and graduate teaching as well as teaching in post-experience and doctoral education. Some programs are taught in Danish, some in English.

Within the Department of Business Humanities and Law, the position will be located in the Governance, Culture and Learning Unit, an interdisciplinary research environment connecting governance studies at all levels of global society. 

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have completed a PhD in intellectual history, history, political sociology, political theory or political philosophy. The candidate will be committed to an academic career, have the capabilities to conduct internationally recognized research and be able to communicate findings clearly. 

The assessment of the candidate will be based primarily on the following qualifications:

• Excellent academic track record
• Research within the history of political, economic or legal thought, political theory, or political philosophy.
• The ability and desire to work autonomously and as part of a team
• Excellent organizational and communication skills (both oral and written); proficiency in English is required

The application (see link below) must include a 3-5-page project description. The project description must include:

The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline. The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment. An appointment committee will invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Appointment

For further information, please contact: PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen, email: mhj.bhl@cbs.dk, or Head of Department Pia Bramming, e-mail pib.bhl@cbs.dk. jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is available from 1 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
Green Biorefinery Pathways for Carbon Capture and Fiber Valorisation into Biobased Materials

Research area and project description:
The transition towards a circular bioeconomy requires new technologies that enable the efficient conversion of biomass into high-value products and long-lived carbon-storing materials. This PhD project will investigate how green biorefinery processing and subsequent pretreatment affect the molecular structure and properties of lignocellulosic fibres from grassland biomass.

The PhD is part of the interdisciplinary research project GrassCO2mposites, which aims to develop novel biobased building materials from grass fibres, linking agricultural biomass production, green biorefining and carbon storage in the built environment.

The research will focus on the processing and detailed characterisation of fibre-rich side streams generated during protein extraction in green biorefineries. Different mechanical, chemical and potentially biological pretreatment methods will be investigated to understand and control changes in the composition, molecular organisation and interactions of key structural biopolymers, including cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin.

Advanced analytical methods will be applied to investigate biopolymer composition, molecular structure, crystallinity, fibre morphology and physicochemical properties. The aim is to establish structure–property relationships that can guide the development of processing methods for producing fibres with tailored characteristics suitable for biobased composite materials.

Experimental work will combine laboratory investigations with pilot- and demonstration-scale processing at Aarhus University's green biorefinery facilities. The PhD will collaborate closely with project partners at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Academy on fibre functionalisation, composite development and material performance.

An additional focus will be to strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration with the Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering at Aarhus University, connecting fundamental biomass processing and biopolymer research with the development and evaluation of biobased construction materials.

The project will contribute new scientific knowledge and scalable processing strategies for the valorisation of agricultural biomass into functional, carbon-storing materials.

Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants must hold a relevant Master's degree (120 ECTS) in chemical engineering, biotechnology, materials science, polymer science or a closely related discipline.

We seek candidates with a strong academic background in lignocellulosic biomass processing, biorefining, polymer chemistry or biobased materials. Experience with experimental processing and characterisation of biomass-derived fibres and biopolymers is particularly relevant.

Knowledge of analytical techniques such as FTIR, NMR, HPLC, GPC/SEC, DSC, TGA, microscopy, rheology or mechanical testing will be considered an advantage. Experience with cellulose extraction, fibre pretreatment, polymer dissolution or other chemical and physicochemical processing methods is also desirable.

Applicants should have strong experimental and analytical skills, an interest in understanding molecular structure–property relationships, and the ability to plan and conduct independent research.

The project requires an interest in interdisciplinary collaboration across chemical engineering, biotechnology and materials science, including collaboration with researchers working on biobased construction materials.

Good written and spoken English communication skills are required. Experience from relevant research projects or industrial R&D will be considered an advantage.

As an OT SCADA Engineer, you will take ownership of SCADA systems and related data flows throughout their lifecycle, from initial analysis and engineering through implementation, operation, improvement and eventual replacement or decommissioning.

You will combine hands-on technical work with structured planning, documentation, and collaboration. Your focus will be on maintaining secure, reliable, and scalable SCADA systems and proactively identifying opportunities to strengthen performance, availability, and operational resilience.

Your responsibilities will include:

• 
Engineering, configuring, commissioning, maintaining, and improving OT SCADA solutions and interfaces for assets in operation and development.

• 
Delivering and supporting reliable data flows from plant-level systems through approved OT integration layers to monitoring, control, analytics, reporting, and data-platform consumers.

• 
Assessing site and interface readiness, identifying integration prerequisites, technical constraints, dependencies, risks and ownership boundaries, and defining requirements and integration approaches.

• 
Configuring, deploying, and supporting resilient SCADA integration components, including industrial edge devices or gateways, connectors, and data pipelines, with appropriate monitoring, troubleshooting, deployment documentation, and operational handover.

• 
Planning, estimating, and tracking assigned work, making dependencies, risks, and progress visible, and documenting and maintaining technical records and operational knowledge.

• 
Providing operational support, including incident diagnosis, service restoration, root-cause and problem analysis, defining and implementing preventive and proactive improvement actions.

• 
Participating in the team's on-call rotation, providing specialist OT SCADA support for business-critical services outside normal working hours.

• 
Improving observability and data quality through health monitoring, completeness checks, alerting, backfilling support, performance analysis, and clear operational ownership.

• 
Planning and executing lifecycle upgrades, migrations, patches, configuration changes, and component replacements using approved change and DTAP practices.

• 
Producing requirements, designs, implementation guides, configuration records, test cases, support documentation, and operational handover packages including operational runbooks, support responsibilities and escalation arrangements

• 
Supporting technical purchasing and supplier coordination through technical evaluations, solution validation, and design reviews.

• 
Preparing and executing tests and commissioning checks for assigned solutions, recording test evidence, tracking defects to resolution, and supporting factory and site acceptance testing (FAT/SAT), acceptance decisions, and operational-readiness assessments.

• 
Standardizing repeatable integration services and work packages for asset projects, while supporting refinement and estimation of less standardized initiatives.

• 
Supporting internal and external audit activities.

Your profile

You hold a relevant bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, automation or control engineering, computer engineering, technical computer science, industrial IT, or a related discipline. Alternatively, you have developed equivalent professional competence through a relevant technical qualification and substantial experience in OT SCADA engineering.

You have several years of hands-on experience engineering, integrating, and supporting SCADA systems or comparable industrial OT solutions, including responsibility for systems in operation. You thrive when taking ownership of solutions from analysis and design through to implementation, operation, and continuous improvement. You are equally comfortable working independently and collaborating with colleagues, suppliers, and stakeholders across the organisation. To succeed in this role, you must have excellent written and spoken English skills. The role may also be subject to security clearance, and candidates must be able to meet the applicable screening requirements.

You bring knowledge and experience in:

• SCADA systems and interfaces: configuring, integrating, commissioning, managing, maintaining, operating, and supporting SCADA applications, gateways, and interfaces connecting operational assets with central systems and data consumers.

• Industrial communications: working with relevant industrial protocols such as OPC UA, IEC 60870-5-104, Modbus TCP or MQTT, as well as APIs and vendor-specific interfaces where applicable, and diagnosing communication and integration issues.

• Operational resilience: practical understanding of high availability, service monitoring and logging, SCADA application and configuration backup and recovery, and configuration management, including dependencies on hosting and network services.

• Operational data flows: understanding signal mapping, timestamps, data quality, buffering, and the recovery of missing historical data.

• Incident and problem management: diagnosing faults across SCADA applications, interfaces, source and target systems, including dependencies on server services, networks, certificates and service accounts; restoring services; investigating root causes; and implementing preventive and proactive improvements.

• Controlled technical changes: planning and delivering upgrades, migrations and configuration changes with appropriate testing, deployment documentation, rollback arrangements and operational handover.

• Secure OT operation: applying OT security requirements, including access controls, certificate handling, system hardening and vulnerability management, within approved architectures and change procedures and in collaboration with cybersecurity and infrastructure teams.

• Engineering documentation: producing and maintaining clear technical documentation of SCADA system architectures, configurations and procedures.

• Supplier collaboration: supporting technical purchasing, assessing and validating solutions, supporting acceptance testing and coordinating technical work with colleagues and external suppliers.

Additional experience that would be valuable:

• Renewable energy, utilities or comparable industrial environments.

• OEM SCADA interfaces.

• Industrial edge platforms or gateways.

• SCADA historians, SQL databases, scripting and automation.

Personal traits

To succeed in this role, we believe that you:

• Bring strong analytical skills, approach technical challenges with proactive, structured problem-solving, and remain composed when resolving operational incidents.

• Communicate clearly and can connect technical, operational and supplier-related perspectives.

• Are comfortable taking end-to-end responsibility, from analysis and planning through implementation and delivery.

• Work independently while contributing actively and collaborating effectively across disciplines with internal and external stakeholders.

• Are organised, reliable and committed to high-quality documentation.

• Take a proactive approach to continuous improvement.

• Use sound judgment to balance immediate service restoration, long-term reliability, maintainability and agreed delivery priorities.

• Are willing to participate in the team’s on-call rotation.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Location: Kolding

Looking for a career with growth?

Looking for a role where your superpowers can be leveraged to the maximum and with limitless opportunities for growth?

The scale and ambition of our wind, battery and solar business means you can really find your element with us. We’ll also provide you with all the learning and development you need to expand your horizons.

We strive to be the best place to work in the industry with highly competitive pay and conditions and an open, supportive culture. A commitment to a healthy work-life balance aims to ensure everyone plays to their strengths, whatever their background and experiences.

You will be part of a growing team of 1,700+ colleagues from 50+ nationalities where our positive approach to diversity is reflected in the fact that more than a quarter of staff are women.

More Information

For more information about the position you are welcome to contact hiring manager Steffen Hellmich, steffen.hellmich@vattenfall.de. For more information about the recruitment process you are welcome to contact our recruiter Christian Pathuel, christian.pathuel@vattenfall.com
